name: infer
description: Inference optimization for any model architecture, on one standard binary. Whatever it was trained as — a CNN, an LSTM, a transformer, a gradient-boosted forest — it arrives here as an ONNX graph, and the passes read the graph rather than the framework, so the same optimizer works on all of them. ONNX is the binary on purpose: onnxruntime executes it on this box and onnxruntime-web executes the same bytes in a browser tab with no second conversion, so what was measured is what ships. Fold constants and fuse operators, strip what only the trainer needed, quantize weights to fp16 or int8 — and get back what each pass actually bought: which operators disappeared, bytes saved, p50/p90/p99 latency before and after on identical inputs, how far the outputs moved and whether the argmax survived. It refuses to flatter itself: quantization regularly makes a small graph SLOWER and the report says so, and the `all` optimization level produces a binary that cannot leave the machine that made it — `portability_lost` names the layout operators that did it and the pass list that avoids them. The console closes the loop by fetching the optimized blob into onnxruntime-web and benchmarking it in the tab, so the browser number comes from a browser instead of an estimate. Fourteen MCP tools, a REST API and the console on one port.

binary.local: onnxruntime — CPU, plus any execution provider this build ships
binary.browser: onnxruntime-web — wasm + SIMD, threads when the page is cross-origin isolated, WebGPU where available
binary.why: one file, two runtimes, no second conversion — the bytes benchmarked here are the bytes the browser runs
binary.verified: a fused model was loaded from /blob and run in onnxruntime-web on 2026-08-29: contrib ops (FusedConv, BiasGelu) ran, com.microsoft.nchwc.Conv did not

passes.slim: strip doc strings, training info and unused initializers (lossless)
passes.shapes: shape inference, so every intermediate tensor is annotated (lossless)
passes.basic: constant folding, dead node and redundant cast/identity elimination (lossless)
passes.extended: basic + operator fusion: Conv+BN, MatMul+Add, GELU, attention (lossless; emits onnxruntime contrib ops, which the browser wasm backend does register)
passes.all: extended + layout transforms for the CPU that ran them (lossless, and genuinely unloadable in a browser: com.microsoft.nchwc.*)
passes.fp16: half-precision weights with fp32 inputs and outputs kept (lossy, ~2x smaller)
passes.int8: dynamic int8 weight quantization, no calibration data needed (lossy, ~4x smaller)
passes.uint8: the same in uint8 — some kernels only have a fast path for one of the two

endpoints.blob: GET /blob/:id — the raw .onnx bytes, what the browser fetches
endpoints.optimize: POST /optimize {model, passes?, batch?, runs?, samples?, tol?}
endpoints.compare: POST /compare {model, passes?} — every pass side by side
endpoints.examples: POST /examples — plant an MLP, a CNN and a transformer block
endpoints.report: POST /report {model, ms, ...} — record what a browser measured
endpoints.reports: GET /reports?model= — browser numbers next to local ones

backend: python: http.server + onnx + onnxruntime (torch only for export)

env.PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 50820)

auth.writes: open on loopback — this module holds models, not keys or money
